stories.headline: Criteria poll shows Kast approval sliding to 36% as two-month mark approaches
stories.summary: The latest Criteria survey (fielded May 7, published May 10) shows President Kast's approval falling two points to 36%, with disapproval stable at 51% and a growing 13% undecided bloc. Kast scores highest on personal attributes (work ethic, directness) but poorly on closeness to citizens, as outlets connect the result to his government's first 60 days in office.

stories.headline: Opposition threatens 'tsunami' of amendments to Kast's flagship reconstruction law as legislative battle escalates
stories.summary: Chile's Plan de Reconstrucción Nacional (megarreforma) became the week's central legislative conflict: a group of opposition deputies announced over 2,000 amendments to slow the bill, Kast accused them of 'boicot,' the Supreme Court flagged legal uncertainty, the Consejo Fiscal Autónomo warned of fiscal risks, and the Partido de la Gente broke from its prior support after negotiations collapsed. Kast also declined to rule out governing by decree if the bill fails.

stories.headline: Chile Vamos friction with Kast intensifies over reconstruction law, Segundo Piso power, and Matthei's public criticism
stories.summary: The governing coalition's relationship with Kast's inner circle became a major political story this week: former presidential candidate Evelyn Matthei (UDI) repeatedly attacked the reconstruction bill's specific measures, prompting counter-attacks from the Partido Republicano and Partido Nacional Libertario; RN senators and deputies raised concerns about presidential visibility and the 'Segundo Piso's' control; and the government convened a conclave at Cerro Castillo to realign Senate votes. Separately, the Partido Republicano and its president Arturo Squella negotiated a 'ceasefire' with the disputed Segundo Piso advisor Irarrázaval.

stories.headline: Kast meets Israeli President Herzog in Costa Rica, announces imminent ambassador restoration
stories.summary: On the sidelines of Costa Rica's presidential inauguration, Kast held a bilateral meeting with Israeli President Isaac Herzog and signaled Chile would restore its ambassador to Israel 'within weeks,' reversing former President Boric's recall of the ambassador in October 2023. The meeting drew criticism from the Chilean Palestinian community and some legislators across the aisle.

stories.headline: Codelco board transition underway as Pacheco exits and Kast prepares new director appointments
stories.summary: With outgoing board chair Máximo Pacheco's mandate ending in late May 2026, Codelco's leadership transition became a major story: Pacheco made a final congressional appearance before the Mining Committee defending the company's direction and its new lithium/copper dual focus, while industry sources reported Kast's government was vetting candidates for the board including Thomas Keller and other industry figures. The Subsecretario de Minería publicly flagged Codelco's debt and safety record as unacceptable.

stories.headline: Gabriel Boric commemorative medal sells out within hours of launch at Casa de Moneda
stories.summary: Chile's Casa de Moneda released a bronze commemorative medal of former President Gabriel Boric on May 6, priced at $27,990 pesos and featuring Braille text for the first time in the series. The edition sold out within hours, generating notable media coverage.

stories.headline: Chilean Navy launches Mes del Mar 2026 with ceremonies nationwide marking 147th anniversary of Iquique
stories.summary: The Armada de Chile officially opened the Mes del Mar 2026 with simultaneous flag-raising ceremonies in Castro, Iquique, Punta Arenas, and Viña del Mar, commemorating the 147th anniversary of the Combate Naval de Iquique and Punta Gruesa and emphasizing Chile's maritime identity and Antarctic presence.

stories.headline: Chilean Armed Forces face budget pressure as strategic funds depleted and domestic deployment costs rise
stories.summary: Multiple reports detail growing financial strain on Chile's armed forces: strategic procurement funds are nearly empty due to delayed transfers, the operational budget has been cut, and the costs of sustained military deployment in the Frontera Norte and Macrozona Sur are compounding the shortfall. An opinion column and a specialist outlet both flag the risk to military readiness.

stories.headline: Carabineros and Army conduct major operation inside Temucuicui in pre-dawn raid
stories.summary: In one of the most significant security operations at the Mapuche community of Temucuicui in years, Carabineros with Army support entered the community before 4am on May 6, 2026. A legislator from the Araucanía region criticized the operation's communication as 'cackling,' while the Temucuicui community itself issued a public communiqué rejecting the raid.

stories.headline: Over 30 scientific societies publish open letter rebuking Kast's 'reductionist' view of research funding
stories.summary: More than 30 Chilean academic and scientific organizations responded to statements by President Kast questioning whether publicly funded research generates concrete employment, publishing an open letter titled 'Ciencia, conocimiento y medio ambiente: bienes que Chile no puede sacrificar.' University of Chile deans and rector candidates joined the critique.

stories.headline: 142 pro-government mayors sign 'Alcaldes comprometidos por Chile' declaration after La Moneda meeting
stories.summary: Following a meeting at the presidential palace, 142 mayors aligned with the governing coalition signed a public declaration supporting Kast's administration, presenting it as a coordination mechanism for local-national governance. Separately, Chile Vamos mayors who attended left frustrated, saying they received no concrete answers on the elimination of the contribuciones (property tax) or rural transport funding.

stories.headline: PDG lawmaker Javier Olivares physically assaulted at sports event; cross-party condemnation follows
stories.summary: Deputy Javier Olivares of the Partido de la Gente reported being punched in the face by a sports club player at an amateur football event in Olmué, Valparaíso region. Legislators from across the political spectrum condemned the attack, with the incident framed politically as connected to tensions over the reconstruction law.

stories.headline: Cabinet fatigue story emerges as Kast resists ministerial reshuffle and Minister Poduje offers self-criticism
stories.summary: Media reported that Kast's cabinet is showing strain at the two-month mark but that the president is resisting changes, fearing any early reshuffle would signal weakness. Housing Minister Iván Poduje, whose confrontational style drew criticism from Chile Vamos and Renovación Nacional, met privately with Kast and offered an autocritique of his 'forms' while standing by his policy positions.

stories.headline: Opposition mobilizes to turn Kast's June 1 Cuenta Pública into an accountability hearing on broken promises
stories.summary: With Kast's first formal congressional address scheduled for June 1, left and center-left parties are coordinating a strategy to use the occasion to highlight unfulfilled campaign commitments. Frente Amplio, the Communist Party, and the Christian Democrats are among those publicly framing the event as a 'juicio' to the administration's first two months.
